answer:
Final answer (natural-language hypothesis):

Across all three disciplines in this 86-study meta-replication dataset, original studies report systematically larger effect sizes than the paired replications on the Fisher-z scale (signed difference d = fiso − fisr; one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank p ≪ 0.001 in every discipline). Quantitatively, percentiles on the signed tally are nearly identical across domains: 88.2% of Social, 82.4% of Cognitive, and 83.3% of Economics studies show fiso > fisr; the corresponding magnitude tally (|fiso| > |fisr|) is also 88.2% / 82.4% / 83.3% — i.e., the 18 replications in which the effect fully reverses sign on the r scale (rr ≤ 0) do not flip the answer because |rr| is consistently smaller than ro even when rr is negative. The domains *most clearly* in this pattern are **Social and Cognitive** (Psychology RPP, n = 34 each), where the median Fisher-z gap d ≈ 0.23–0.25 (Wilcoxon one-sided p ≈ 10⁻⁶); **Economics** (EERP, n = 18) shows a smaller but still clearly positive median gap (d = 0.143, one-sided p = 4 × 10⁻⁴). Pairwise Mann–Whitney comparisons on d are not significant after Benjamini–Hochberg correction (Soc vs Cog p_BH = 0.58, Soc vs Econ p_BH = 0.58, Cog vs Econ p_BH = 0.71), and the Kruskal–Wallis omnibus is H = 1.25 (p = 0.54), so we do not have statistical evidence that the original-replication gap differs across disciplines. Bottom line: originals exceed replications in *every* domain (Social, Cognitive, Economics), the typical Fisher-z gap is on the order of 0.23 (≈0.10–0.15 on the correlation scale), and **no domain exhibits the reverse pattern**.

Supporting per-domain table:

| discipline | project.x | n | n_rr≤0 | median d | IQR d | mean d | sd d | % fiso>fisr | % \|fiso\|>\|fisr\| | Wilcoxon one-sided p(d>0) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Social | Psychology | 34 | 10 | +0.232 | 0.282 | +0.233 | 0.203 | 88.2% | 88.2% | 5.8e-07 |
| Cognitive | Psychology | 34 | 5 | +0.249 | 0.389 | +0.289 | 0.359 | 82.4% | 82.4% | 3.2e-06 |
| Economics | Experimental Economics | 18 | 3 | +0.143 | 0.256 | +0.266 | 0.365 | 83.3% | 83.3% | 4.2e-04 |

Pairwise Mann–Whitney (two-sided p, BH-adjusted): Social vs Cognitive (U=548, p_two=0.713, p_BH=0.580), Social vs Economics (U=364, p_two=0.265, p_BH=0.580), Cognitive vs Economics (U=351, p_two=0.387, p_BH=0.713). Kruskal–Wallis omnibus: H=1.248, p=0.536. Overall: median d_signed = +0.229; 84.9% of all 86 studies have fiso > fisr (signed tally equals magnitude tally to one decimal).

payload.workflow: Loaded /workspace/data/meta-regression_joined_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv (86 rows × 60 columns). Dropped fully-null columns (aggregated, lab_id) and the redundant n.r column (used nr per agreement). Computed per-study signed contrast d_signed = fiso − fisr on the Fisher-z scale, plus magnitude contrast d_mag = |fiso| − |fisr|. Identified rr ≤ 0 (18 rows — Social 10, Cognitive 5, Economics 3) as sign-flipped replications; flagged but kept in the signed tally per the brief and excluded in the magnitude-exclude variant. Grouped by discipline (Social/Cognitive/Economics). For each domain reported n, median+IQR of d, mean±SD of d, % fiso > fisr, % |fiso| > |fisr|, one-sample Wilcoxon signed-rank against H₁: d>0 (one-sided), pairwise Mann–Whitney two-sided with Benjamini–Hochberg correction across the 3 pairs, and Kruskal–Wallis omnibus. Saved results_table.csv and hypothesis.md.
